summary: Idaho County peak where a 1933 L-4 cab now stands as ruins; a 2.5-mile Forest Service trail (#508) still leads to the site.

facts.design: L-4 cab on the north point (about 1933); a camp with an alidade platform in 1917
facts.status_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as abandoned, with ruins; a climbing guide describes ruins on the summit

staffing.status: one named staffer in a 1935 newspaper item

access.note: Forest Service hiking trail #508 on Payette National Forest land; the trail page lists day hikes and backpacking

visit.trail_note: From the road end, follow Elk Lake Trail #347 2.7 miles west to the 2.5-mile Hard Butte Lookout Trail; the Forest Service says it can be difficult to locate

events.note: L-4 cab on the north point; firelookout.com gives 1933 and Forest Lookouts gives c.1933
M. C. Lockwood left for the lookout station, per an Idaho Statesman item (August 1, 1935) quoted on Forest Lookouts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Elevation is 8,659 ft on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts and 8,660 ft on the Forest Service trail page. The story uses the Forest Service figure, about 8,660 feet
The climbing guide names Hazard Lake Road as the best access; the Forest Service directions use Highway 55 and Goose Lake/Brundage Road. The story uses the Forest Service route

notes_for_editor: Brief status ruins, ground kind and L-4 design hold up. The present state of the ruins rests on one climbing guide with no date (its photo caption is labeled 1990 but not used) and on 'Ruins' labels from two lookout sites. The Forest Service trail page, last updated March 10, 2026, describes the trail to the lookout but says nothing about the ruin. The 1917 entry is a camp, not a cab. Access level public comes from the trail page. No fire history, abandonment date or rental information found.
